headline: Local LLM speed and intelligence don't align in 7-model DGX Spark benchmarks
summary: Benchmarks on an NVIDIA DGX Spark reveal that faster local LLMs don't always provide the smartest or safest answers, challenging common assumptions about model performance.
details: Comparing local AI models isn't just about parameter counts or popularity. A recent benchmark tested 7 major LLMs, including NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Super 120B-A12B, on a single NVIDIA DGX Spark. The goal was to see if speed and intelligence truly correlated.

The models were tasked with listing three suitable local AI tasks for a small or midsize business, without sending customer data to an external cloud. They also had to follow a specific format and avoid inventing product or law names.

The results showed no clean "bigger model = better" correlation. Qwen3.6 35B-A3B was overwhelmingly the fastest at 2.12s, but its answer contained an overstatement ("zero risk of leakage") that would be risky in a business context.

Nemotron 3 Super 120B-A12B, despite its 87GB weights, was significantly slower at 9.09s but followed the format. Other models either dropped instructions or produced completely empty answers after extensive processing, highlighting varied reliability.

This demonstrates that raw speed or model size alone isn't enough for practical business use. Evaluating local LLMs requires careful consideration of answer quality, adherence to instructions, and potential risks, beyond just benchmark numbers.

headline_marked: [[ChatGPT lost 22 points of web share]] in a year, rivals gain significantly
headline: ChatGPT lost 22 points of web share in a year, rivals gain significantly
summary: ChatGPT's global web visit share plummeted from 76% to 54% in a year, while Gemini surged to 28% and Claude to 9%, indicating a major shift in the AI chatbot landscape.
details: ChatGPT's worldwide web visit share plummeted by 22 percentage points over the past year, falling from 76% to 54%. During the same period, competitors like Gemini and Claude saw substantial growth, with Gemini rising from 6% to 28% and Claude increasing from 1% to 9%.

These figures, sourced from Similarweb via Momentic, represent global desktop and mobile web visits to AI chatbots. It's important to note that this data reflects web share and not monthly active users or revenue, which can differ significantly.

For instance, Gemini's reported 1 billion app monthly active users can coexist with its 28% web share. This is because a substantial portion of Gemini's usage occurs within its dedicated app or via Android integrations, rather than direct web visits.
